p: You already know what a grey looks like even if you've never read a UFO book. They're short, usually three or four feet tall, with skinny arms and legs and a small body. The head is way too big for the rest of it, with a narrow chin, a little slit for a mouth, two small holes for a nose and no real ears. And then the eyes, which are the part everybody remembers. Huge, black and almond-shaped, wrapping around the sides of the head with no white and no pupil.

Witnesses usually say they're hairless and either wear nothing or a tight suit, and that they talk without actually speaking. A lot of abduction stories also have a taller grey in charge, sometimes described as a leader or a doctor.

sections.h: How the grey became the face of aliens
p: Before the 1960s people reported all kinds of visitors. Tall blond humans, hairy little guys, robots, glowing figures, you name it. The grey took over after Betty and Barney Hill said they were taken aboard a craft in New Hampshire on the night of September 19, 1961. Under hypnosis in 1964 they described small beings with big wraparound eyes. We have the [full Betty and Barney Hill story](/encounters/betty-barney-hill-1961/) if you want the details.

Betty also drew a star map she said she was shown on board. An Ohio schoolteacher named Marjorie Fish spent years building a 3D model of nearby stars to match it and decided it pointed to the double star Zeta Reticuli, which is why greys get called Zeta Reticulans.

Movies and books did the rest. The aliens in Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) were slim and big-eyed, and Whitley Strieber put a painted grey face on the cover of his 1987 bestseller Communion. After that the grey was basically the official alien on T-shirts, posters and TV, The X-Files included.

The look took shape in the US but the same beings show up in abduction and close encounter reports from Canada, Britain, Australia, Brazil and plenty of other places. Travis Walton, the Arizona logger who went missing for five days in 1975, described short beings with big dark eyes too. Our [close encounters](/encounters/) section has cases from all over.

Believers take that as a sign people are seeing something real. Sceptics say it just shows how fast one image spreads once it's on every movie poster and book cover. I can see it both ways to be honest, which doesn't happen to me very often.

Researcher Martin Kottmeyer found an episode of The Outer Limits called "The Bellero Shield" with an alien that had big wraparound eyes. It aired on February 10, 1964 and Barney Hill first described the beings' eyes under hypnosis twelve days later. Kottmeyer's take was that the episode could have shaped the memory without Barney ever realising it.

The big-headed, big-eyed human of the far future was also a science fiction idea long before 1961, going back to at least H. G. Wells's 1893 essay "The Man of the Year Million". Psychologists add that a lot of abduction memories came out under hypnosis, which can give you vivid memories that aren't reliable, and that sleep paralysis can leave people sure there were small figures standing around the bed. If you've ever had sleep paralysis you know how real that feels.

faq.a: Greys or Grays mostly. They also get called Zeta Reticulans, after the star system tied to Betty Hill's star map, and sometimes Roswell greys. UFO books also use EBE, short for extraterrestrial biological entity.

faq.q: Where are grey aliens supposed to come from?
faq.a: The best-known claim is Zeta Reticuli, a pair of stars about 39 light years away, based on Marjorie Fish's take on Betty Hill's star map. There's no evidence anybody lives there.

Nobody has ever proven a grey exists and there's no physical evidence. Thousands of people sincerely describe meeting them though. The usual explanations are sleep paralysis, memories shaped by hypnosis and the influence of movies and book covers.

faq.q: What is the difference between greys and Nordics?
faq.a: Greys are short, hairless and big-eyed and mostly show up in abduction stories from the 1960s on. Nordics are tall, blond and look human, and they come out of the 1950s contactee era. Have a look at [grey aliens vs Nordic aliens](/compare/grey-aliens-vs-nordic-aliens/) and our [Nordic aliens](/creatures/nordic-aliens/) page.

faq.q: Why do grey aliens have big black eyes?
faq.a: That's how witnesses describe them, and the Hill case and the Communion cover locked the look in. Some believers think the black eyes are lenses or some kind of covering. Sceptics point out that science fiction was drawing advanced beings with big eyes and big heads long before 1961.
